reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that non-leaders possess and exercise agency. The passage shows common workers, young men (נְעָרַי), and ordinary people (יֶתֶר הָעָ֔ם) actively building the wall, standing guard with weapons, making decisions about their positions, responding to organizational directives, and participating in defense efforts. Nehemiah specifically addresses both leaders (חֹרִים, סְגָנִים) and 'the rest of the people,' with all groups taking meaningful action. The text states the people carried swords and worked with agency: 'בְּאַחַ֤ת יָדוֹ֙ עֹשֶׂ֣ה בַמְּלָאכָ֔ה וְאַחַ֖ת מַחֲזֶ֥קֶת הַשָּׁלַח' (with one hand working and one hand holding the weapon). This contradicts the exclusive attribution of agency to leaders alone.
